paragraphs.notes: Markush enumeration table, recorded as one paragraph per the pass instructions. The cells are compound numbers and substituent symbols, not German prose, so zh and en are the same string; the only German-language token on the page is the column head 'Nr.' (Nummer, i.e. No.), left as printed so the header row matches the source. The page carries no Tabelle caption and no scaffold drawing: it opens mid-sequence at Nr. 476, so the shared substituents that caption fixes are set on an earlier page and are not visible here. Column heads are printed with superscripts, R with a raised 1, 2 and 3; transcribed inline as R1, R2, R3. Subscript digits in SO2, CF3 and (CH2)2 are printed as true subscripts and transcribed inline. The R1 cell of rows 476 to 480 carries a small drawn ring instead of text; each is recorded in drawings and the cell is marked in the transcription with a pointer to the matching drawings entry, rather than with a name the drawing does not itself write. The R1 column changes value inside the page: 476 to 480 are the drawn fragment, 481 to 489 read O(CH2)2O(CH2)2OMe and 490 to 498 read O(CH2)2O(CH2)2OEt. A small ink blot sits in the R3 cell of Nr. 476, well to the right of and below the CF3; it reads as a scan artifact, not a character. A faint dot sits in the left margin beside Nr. 485 and another beside the R1 cell of Nr. 492; both are scan artifacts. The table body ends after Nr. 498 and the foot of the page below the table is blank.

drawings.notes: Belongs to row Nr. 476; it is that row's R1 value, drawn instead of written. The ring is drawn flat with no wedge or hash, so the configuration at C2 is not specified by the drawing. smiles is null because the fragment as drawn has an open valence at the attachment oxygen and no attachment-point notation is used elsewhere in this run; writing OCC1CCCO1 would assert a hydroxyl that the drawing does not show. The same fragment is drawn in the R1 cell of each of rows 476 to 480 on this page.
